title: One complete round of the split search
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $start$ be one of its states, let $w,s,out$ be Boolean words, and let $T\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that, from the source configuration with state $start$, unary work tapes of length $|s|+1$, heads at $0$, and empty output, the source machine on empty input reaches the halted configuration with those same work tapes and output $out$ after $T$ steps. Then there is a natural number $t$ with $0<t\le T+5|s|+3|w|+20$ such that at every time $j$ with $0<j<t$ the round body, started on input $w$ from its anchor configuration with candidate $s$, is not in the anchor state. If $|s|+|out|=|w|$, the configuration at time $t$ is halted and its output is the encoding formed by doubling each bit of the prefix of $w$ of length $|s|$, then appending $01$, then appending the remaining suffix of $w$. Otherwise, the configuration at time $t$ is the anchor configuration with candidate $s$ extended by one bit $1$ when $|s|\le |w|$, and with candidate $s$ unchanged when $|s|>|w|$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
The source run from the specified unary-tape initial configuration halts after $T$ steps with output $out$ and the same work tapes
replaced:
Suppose the source machine, started on the prepared bank for candidate $s$,
reaches the halted bank with output $o$ after $T$ steps. Then there is a time
$t$ with $0 < t \le T + 5\abs{s} + 3\abs{w} + 20$ such that the round body,
started from the canonical anchored configuration carrying $s$ on input $w$,
never revisits the anchor strictly between times $0$ and $t$, and at time
$t$: if $\abs{s} + \abs{o} = \abs{w}$ the body has halted with output the
pair encoding of the split of $w$ at position $\abs{s}$; otherwise the body
is back at the canonical anchored configuration carrying one split-search
step applied to $s$.
